headline: OpenAI opened a public beta of its Decisions API, which lets developers get fast, structured answers such as classifications and routing choices from its GPT-6 Luna model.
score_reason: Developer-facing beta; speed claim is OpenAI's and general release is still weeks away.
importance_line: Developers can add quick sorting and routing decisions to apps at low cost, but the speed claim is OpenAI's own and the product is still in beta.
summary: Unite.AI reports, citing OpenAI's changelog and documentation, that OpenAI released its Decisions API in public beta on 6 Oct 2026, an interface that answers developer-set questions about text and images with a probability, a pick from fixed options or a score. OpenAI says it is about 10 times faster than its Responses API and costs $0.10 per million input tokens, with general availability expected in the coming weeks.
notes: Read at Unite.AI, which cites OpenAI's changelog and docs; source credited to OpenAI via Unite.AI.
